selectionReason: A real Flask application with a historical named-configuration path escape, pinned source and a narrow repair region; selected before scanner or agent outcomes.
task: The named configuration route uses a request parameter as a filesystem path, allowing reads and writes outside the configured storage directory. Reject names containing path separators or characters outside the existing letters, digits, underscore, period, plus, and hyphen contract instead of silently rewriting them. Preserve the exact accepted name, unnamed configuration changes, valid named save and load behavior, redirects, sessions, and the existing configuration-disable policy. Keep existing tests unchanged.
limitations: This public historical fix may have appeared in model training.
The reference copies only the upstream named-configuration route and required import; unrelated URL-validation changes from the same commit are excluded.
Qualification uses Flask's real test client and controlled benign pickle dictionaries; it does not exercise deserialization of untrusted object types.
The upstream requirements omit Flask's transitive Blinker dependency, so the runtime resolves transitive releases no newer than the pinned source commit and verifies the resulting lock digest.
The Stem package has no wheel. Its hash-locked source release is the only dependency built during runtime preparation.
Local configuration route checks run offline. Upstream tests that perform live search requests are outside this case.
The runtime uses standalone Python 3.11.13, not every deployment image supported by Whoogle.
This case is not part of the completed 45-assignment pilot. Any model run belongs to a new, separately registered batch.
Scanner misses remain recorded; they do not disqualify or replace cases.
